grading.extraCredit: Students with fewer than three unexcused absences get extra credit toward the final grade; the amount is not stated.

materials.item: No required textbook; readings on eLC

PBHL 3100.attendance: Strongly encouraged and tracked on TopHat, which starts after drop/add ends; excused absences (health, religious, campus organization) waive that day's TopHat questions.
other: Absences must be excused by the instructor within a reasonable time, with documentation as appropriate.
An honors option exists for eligible students through an extra paper or project.

other: UGA policy bars AI for coursework unless the instructor allows it; in this course AI may help with brainstorming, outlines, grammar and study guides.
AI may not be used to write assignments, answer quiz or test questions, or paste generated content into submissions; any AI use should be cited.
Sources used, especially for the group project, must be cited in a consistent style.

objectives: Students will be able to articulate concepts of health and public health and convey their value and importance to clients and the public.
Students will be able to identify field placement opportunities based on students' skills, qualifications, and interests.
Students will be able to identify field expectations that align with MPH and concentration competencies.
Students will be able to examine and detail learning outcomes mapped to appropriate competency attainment through the proposed Applied Practice Experience.
Students will be able to examine the structure and functions of a relevant public health agency.
Students will be able to examine the public health impact of the agency’s mission, vision, and values.
Students will be able to develop and refine a comprehensive proposal for the Applied Practice Experience.
Students will be able to manage assessments and professional development tools and resources to attain placement at an APE site and support future career goals.
